title_en: Bank of Communications, Zhongshan Sub-branch v. China Complete Plant Export Corporation Wuhan Branch Business Office, People's Construction Bank of China, Haikou Branch, et al. — retrial of dispute over bank acceptance drafts
keywords_en: Civil; Negotiable Instrument Dispute; Retrial; Supreme People's Court; Guangdong Province; Hubei Province; Hainan Province; Legal Person; Financial Institution; Civil Procedure Law; Lawful Acquisition of Bank Acceptance Draft; Bona Fide Possession; Right of Recourse on Negotiable Instrument; Reversal of Judgment; Bank Acceptance Draft; Discounting; Fraud; Bank Acceptance Draft Dispute Involving Branches, etc.
full_text_en:
Petitioner (Original Defendant): Business Office of Wuhan Branch, China National Complete Plant Export Corporation

Legal Representative: Lin Changbo, Manager

Petitioner (Original Defendant): Haikou Branch, People's Construction Bank of China

Legal Representative: Zhao Honglin, President

Respondent (Original Plaintiff): Zhongshan Branch, Bank of Communications

Legal Representative: Ma Fengwu, Manager

Third Party at First Instance: Hainan Wanda Industry and Trade Company

Third Party at First Instance: Former Central South Aviation Enterprise Group

The petitioners, Business Office of Wuhan Branch, China National Complete Plant Export Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the Business Office) and Haikou Branch, People's Construction Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Haikou Construction Bank), dissatisfied with the civil judgment that had taken legal effect rendered by the Intermediate People's Court of Zhongshan City, Guangdong Province, in a dispute over bank acceptance drafts with Zhongshan Branch, Bank of Communications (hereinafter referred to as Zhongshan Bank of Communications), Hainan Wanda Industry and Trade Group Company (hereinafter referred to as Wanda Company), and the Former Central South Aviation Enterprise Group (hereinafter referred to as the Former Central South Aviation), filed a petition with the Supreme People's Court. The Supreme People's Court, pursuant to Article 187 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled to accept the case for retrial.

The judgment of the Intermediate People's Court of Zhongshan City found: Upon the application of Zhongshan Petrochemical Steel Pipe Factory (hereinafter referred to as the Steel Pipe Factory), Zhongshan Bank of Communications issued on February 19, 1990, nine bank acceptance drafts numbered 0000207-0000215, with a total face value of RMB 80 million and an acceptance period of nine months. Among them, the total face value of the bank acceptance drafts with the Former Central South Aviation as the payee was RMB 30 million; the total face value of the bank acceptance drafts with the Business Office and the Business Department of Wuhan Branch, China National Complete Plant Export Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the Business Department, which is the same organization with two names) as payees was RMB 25 million each. After the Former Central South Aviation obtained three bank acceptance drafts each with a face value of RMB 10 million, it discounted one of them and endorsed the other two over to Wanda Company, which discounted the said two bank acceptance drafts with Haikou Construction Bank on July 22, 1990. The three bank acceptance drafts with a total face value of RMB 25 million held by the Business Department had been returned to Zhongshan Bank of Communications. The original judgment held: Shenzhen Shidelishi Stone Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenshi Company) and the Former Central South Aviation, by inducing banks and enterprises with the promise of helping them obtain interbank funds, and by signing economic contracts to fraudulently obtain bank acceptance drafts, had constituted fraudulent conduct. The Former Central South Aviation should return to Zhongshan Bank of Communications the proceeds from discounting the fraudulently obtained draft numbered 0000210 with a face value of RMB 10 million at Hankou Branch, Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Hankou Bank of China), plus bank interest for the period of illegal possession. Haikou Construction Bank, after being deceived by the Former Central South Aviation, forced the Former Central South Aviation to endorse and transfer the RMB 20 million bank acceptance drafts to Wanda Company in violation of regulations, and Wanda Company then discounted the RMB 20 million bank acceptance drafts; therefore, Haikou Construction Bank's possession of the drafts had no legal basis. Haikou Construction Bank knew that the drafts were fraudulently obtained by the Former Central South Aviation and that the drafts were not based on legal commodity transactions, but it still processed the discount in violation of laws and relevant regulations; its discounting conduct was illegal and should not be protected by state law. Haikou Construction Bank should return the illegally possessed drafts to Zhongshan Bank of Communications. The Business Office became the payee of the bank acceptance drafts based on a joint venture agreement signed with Shenshi Company; since the joint venture agreement was invalid, the drafts obtained by the Business Office under the invalid contract should be returned. Furthermore, after receiving the RMB 25 million bank acceptance drafts provided by Shenshi Company, the Business Office did not pay the corresponding consideration, and despite knowing that the drafts were obtained by Shenshi Company through fraudulent means, it still refused to return the drafts to Zhongshan Bank of Communications, constituting malicious possession. The court ruled: 1. The conduct of the defendant Business Office and the defendant Haikou Construction Bank in illegally holding the bank acceptance drafts issued by the plaintiff Zhongshan Bank of Communications is confirmed as invalid civil acts. 2. The plaintiff Zhongshan Bank of Communications shall not accept the drafts under the three bank acceptance drafts issued on February 19, 1990, with the defendant Business Office as the payee, numbered 0000208, 0000214, 0000215, totaling RMB 25 million, and the drafts under the two bank acceptance drafts with the Third Party Former Central South Aviation as the payee (currently held by Haikou Construction Bank), numbered 0000209, 0000211, totaling RMB 20 million. The defendant Business Office and Haikou Construction Bank shall return all the said acceptance drafts held by them to the plaintiff Zhongshan Bank of Communications within five days from the date this judgment takes legal effect. 3. The proceeds of RMB 10 million obtained by the Third Party Former Central South Aviation from discounting the bank acceptance draft numbered 0000210 issued by the plaintiff with Hankou Bank of China, together with the bank interest payable for the period of illegal possession (calculated at 0.05% per day on the unpaid amount from November 19, 1990, until the date of full repayment), shall be returned to the plaintiff within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect. The case acceptance fee of RMB 285,010 and other litigation costs of RMB 22,520, totaling RMB 307,530, shall be borne by Zhongshan Bank of Communications in the amount of RMB 17,530, by the Business Office in the amount of RMB 131,818, by Haikou Construction Bank in the amount of RMB 105,455, and by the Former Central South Aviation in the amount of RMB 52,727.

The Business Office and Haikou Construction Bank, dissatisfied with the judgment of the Intermediate People's Court of Zhongshan City, filed a petition with the Supreme People's Court. The Business Office claimed: It obtained the RMB 25 million bank acceptance drafts lawfully, possessed them in good faith, and had the right to claim payment from the acceptor of the drafts; the lawsuit filed by Zhongshan Bank of Communications was not consistent with the facts and lacked legal basis. Haikou Construction Bank claimed: Wanda Company transferred the RMB 20 million bank acceptance drafts to it through discounting, and it was a lawful holder of the drafts; Zhongshan Bank of Communications should pay the draft amount.

Upon retrial, the Supreme People's Court found: Li Shaoming and others from Zhuhai Jade Gem Jewelry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jade Company) promised Zhongshan Bank of Communications that if Zhongshan Bank of Communications issued bank acceptance drafts totaling RMB 80 million to Jade Company, Jade Company could introduce RMB 80 million in funds from elsewhere and provide half of it for Zhongshan Bank of Communications' use. To convince Zhongshan Bank of Communications that funds could indeed be introduced, Jade Company also provided Zhongshan Bank of Communications with the Joint Venture Agreement No. (90)001 signed between Shenshi Company and the Business Department, and relevant materials from the Former Central South Aviation, including Letter No. (Hang) (Han) Zi 019 and Letter No. (Hang) (Han) Zi 020, which stated that the Former Central South Aviation could provide funds to Shenshi Company. After review, Zhongshan Bank of Communications agreed to Jade Company's request and issued on February 19, 1990, nine bank acceptance drafts with the Steel Pipe Factory as the applicant, a total face value of RMB 80 million, and an acceptance period of nine months. Among them, three drafts—No. 0000207 with a face value of RMB 5 million, and Nos. 0000212 and 0000213 each with a face value of RMB 10 million—had the Business Department as the payee; three drafts—No. 0000205 with a face value of RMB 5 million, and Nos. 0000214 and 0000215 each with a face value of RMB 10 million—had the Business Office as the payee; and three drafts—Nos. 0000209, 0000210, and 0000211 each with a face value of RMB 10 million—had the Former Central South Aviation as the payee. To this end, Jade Company and the Steel Pipe Factory signed an investment joint venture contract on March 8 of the same year, and Zhongshan Bank of Communications, as the Steel Pipe Factory's bank, also signed and stamped the contract. Jade Company and the Steel Pipe Factory also agreed in the joint venture contract that the bank acceptance drafts used to perform this agreement should not be discounted or transferred, except for reasons of force majeure and with the consent of the issuing bank. The above drafts issued by Zhongshan Bank of Communications were handed over by the Steel Pipe Factory to Jade Company, which then gave them to Shenshi Company. Shenshi Company delivered the drafts to the payees—the Business Department, the Business Office, and the Former Central South Aviation—on March 3 and March 16 of the same year, respectively. After the Former Central South Aviation obtained the five bank acceptance drafts numbered 0000209, 0000210, and 0000211, it applied for discount of the draft numbered 0000210 with a face value of RMB 10 million at Hankou Bank of China. Hankou Bank of China processed the discount of the RMB 10 million bank acceptance draft for the Former Central South Aviation on March 15, 1990. On June 12, 1990, the Former Central South Aviation endorsed and transferred the bank acceptance drafts numbered 0000209 and 0000211, each with a face value of RMB 10 million, to Wanda Company. On July 22 of the same year, Wanda Company and Haikou Construction Bank signed a "Draft Discount Agreement" and delivered the above two drafts to Haikou Construction Bank. Because a working group from the head office of the People's Construction Bank of China was then inspecting Haikou Construction Bank, and based on the working group's opinion that accepted drafts should not be paid temporarily until the draft verification work was completed and then funds should be transferred, Haikou Construction Bank did not transfer the funds to Wanda Company's account until November 10 of the same year in accordance with the discount agreement. Additionally, on July 18 of the same year, Haikou Construction Bank had asked the Hainan Branch of the People's Bank of China to inquire about the above two drafts, and on July 25, Zhongshan Bank of Communications replied by telegram, requesting that the drafts not be discounted. It was also found: On January 25, 1990, Shenshi Company and the Business Department signed a Joint Venture Agreement No. (Chu) Lian Zi (001). Pursuant to this joint venture agreement, Shenshi Company delivered bank acceptance drafts totaling RMB 50 million to the Business Department and the Business Office. After receiving the drafts, the two offices issued a receipt in the name of the Business Department. Subsequently, after repeated requests by Zhongshan Bank of Communications, the Business Department returned the three drafts numbered 0000207, 0000212, and 0000213 to Zhongshan Bank of Communications on June 12, 1990. After receiving the three drafts numbered 0000208, 0000214, and 0000215, the Business Office requested Shenshi Company to provide confirmation from Zhongshan Bank of Communications regarding the issued drafts. On March 7 and March 8, 1990, Zhongshan Bank of Communications sent two confirmation letters to Wuhan Branch, China National Complete Plant Export Corporation, stating "confirmation, payment upon maturity." After receiving the confirmation letters, the Business Office, pursuant to the joint venture agreement, paid funds, delivered goods, and settled debts totaling RMB 18,548,230 to Shenshi Company and its designated entities.

The Supreme People's Court held: A bill is a formal instrument, and its textual nature and independence are important characteristics. The nine bank acceptance drafts issued and accepted by Zhongshan Bank of Communications, with the Business Office, Business Department, and Former Central South Aviation as payees and a total face value of RMB 80 million, were complete in form and contained all essential elements, making them valid drafts. Although the "Bank Settlement Measures" issued by the People's Bank of China stipulate that the issuance of commercial drafts must be based on legal commodity transactions, this is not a provision on the validity of the drafts. The existence of a bill relationship is not premised on the establishment and validity of the underlying relationship; the bill relationship and its underlying relationship are relatively independent. Zhongshan Bank of Communications' claim that the drafts it issued and accepted were invalid because there was no legal commodity transaction and because it was deceived lacks legal basis. The Former Central South Aviation was the payee of three drafts. Although Jade Company, the Steel Pipe Factory, and Zhongshan Bank of Communications agreed in the investment joint venture contract that the bank acceptance drafts issued by Zhongshan Bank of Communications should not be transferred or discounted, this agreement does not bind payees who are not parties to the contract. Additionally, Zhongshan Bank of Communications used old-style drafts at the time, which contained a notation prohibiting circulation and transfer; however, the new bank settlement measures then in effect permitted endorsement and transfer of drafts, and the People's Bank of China allowed the temporary use of old-style drafts. Therefore, the notation had become invalid, and the endorsement and transfer of the two drafts by the Former Central South Aviation in this case were valid. After the Former Central South Aviation endorsed and transferred the two bank acceptance drafts, each with a face value of RMB 10 million, to Wanda Company, Wanda Company became the lawful holder of the drafts. On July 22, 1990, Wanda Company and Haikou Construction Bank signed a "Discount Agreement" and delivered the acceptance drafts to Haikou Construction Bank; therefore, although Haikou Construction Bank did not transfer the funds into Wanda Company's account until November 10 of the same year due to other reasons, it should still be determined that Wanda Company had discounted the two bank acceptance drafts it held on July 22. As the lawful holder of the drafts, Haikou Construction Bank has the right to assert its rights under the drafts against Zhongshan Bank of Communications, and Zhongshan Bank of Communications should pay the draft amounts. The Business Office was the payee of the three bank acceptance drafts issued by Zhongshan Bank of Communications. After receiving the drafts, it paid RMB 18,548,230 to Shenshi Company; therefore, it should be determined that the Business Office paid the corresponding consideration for obtaining the RMB 25 million acceptance drafts. The Business Office is the lawful holder of the RMB 25 million acceptance drafts, and Zhongshan Bank of Communications should pay the draft amounts.

In summary, Zhongshan Bank of Communications is obligated to unconditionally pay the drafts it issued and accepted, which are complete in form and contain all essential elements, upon maturity. The endorsement chain of the drafts discounted by Haikou Construction Bank is continuous; the Business Office, as the payee of the RMB 25 million bank acceptance drafts, has paid the corresponding consideration; both are lawful holders of the acceptance drafts. Pursuant to Article 84, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "a creditor has the right to demand that the debtor perform his obligations as specified by the contract or as provided by law," and with reference to Article 3, Paragraph 3 of the "Interim Measures for the Acceptance and Discount of Commercial Drafts" issued by the People's Bank of China, which provides that "after the draft is accepted, the acceptor is obligated to unconditionally pay the draft amount upon maturity," and Article 14, Paragraph 9, Subparagraph (3) of the "Bank Settlement Measures," which provides that "upon maturity of the discount, the discounting bank shall collect the draft amount from the accepting bank," Haikou Construction Bank and the Business Office, as creditors under the bank acceptance drafts, have the right to assert their rights under the drafts against Zhongshan Bank of Communications. The original judgment's determination that the payees, endorsers, and endorsee of the said bank acceptance drafts illegally held the bank acceptance drafts, and its order for the holders to return the bank acceptance drafts they held to Zhongshan Bank of Communications, are erroneous and should be reversed. Accordingly, on July 5, 1994, the Supreme People's Court, pursuant to Article 177, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment:

1. The civil judgment (Zhong Zhong Fa Jing Zi [1990] No. 51) of the Intermediate People's Court of Zhongshan City, Guangdong Province, is hereby reversed;

2. The claims of Zhongshan Branch, Bank of Communications are hereby dismissed.

The original case acceptance fee and other litigation costs, totaling RMB 307,530, shall be borne by Zhongshan Branch, Bank of Communications.
